title: Client Assessment Response Playbook — Logs, Roles & SIEM
body:
Purpose: Quick, reviewable playbook for responding to customer security questionnaires that ask about role-based access control (RBAC v2), audit log schema and retention, SIEM export options, and evidence automation. Built to be used by solutions engineering, sales security leads, and product security reviewers.

Scope: Focuses on the canonical questions we see during RFP/questionnaire processes: who can do what, what events we log, how logs are exported to customer SIEMs, where evidence lives, and how to automate delivery. This is NOT the full architecture doc — link to the full RBAC design and audit-log spec in linked_artifacts.

Quick usage instructions:
1) Read the canned answers below and pick the ones that match the customer's deployment mode (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private).
2) Attach the named evidence files referenced in the Attachments section.
3) For any custom SIEM mapping requests, open a ticket to SEC-OPS and include the customer Syslog/CEF/format sample.

Canned responses (short-form, copy-paste friendly):
- "Do you support RBAC?"
  Recommended answer: "Yes. Redwood implements RBAC v2: role definitions are declarative and bound to identities via project-level and organization-level policies. Roles are principle-of-least-privilege by default; commonly used roles include admin, infra-operator, model-deployer, read-only-analyst, and billing-viewer. Role assignments and changes are recorded in the audit log and subject to the change-review workflow for Dedicated and Private customers."

- "How are audit logs produced and what do they contain?"
  Recommended answer: "We emit structured JSON audit events for control-plane and data-plane actions. Events include timestamp (RFC3339), actor (user/service account id and source IP), action (canonical action name), target (resource id and type), request metadata (request id, route, model version), result (success/failure, error code), and optional payloads (truncated request/response hashes). For Hosted customers, logs are stored in our encrypted telemetry service and retained based on plan; Dedicated and Private options support customer-managed retention and direct forwarding."

- "Can we export logs to our SIEM?"
  Recommended answer: "Yes. Supported export modes: secure syslog (TLS), S3/HTTPS export (parquet/ndjson), and an event-push webhook for near-real-time delivery. We also provide a CEF translation layer for customers that require security-device parsing. Exports can be configured via the Console with filters (by project, model, action, severity) and batching cadence. For Dedicated/Private, we can route directly into customer VPC endpoints."

- "How long do you retain audit logs?"
  Recommended answer: "Default retention for Hosted is 90 days for audit events and 365 days for critical security events; retention is configurable for Dedicated customers and fully customer-controlled for Private deployments. Retention policies are enforced by the telemetry service and are documented in the retention manifest we provide during assessments."

Evidence pointers (files to attach depending on ask):
- audit-log-sample-ndjson.txt — 50 lines of representative audit events (anonymized).
- rbac-role-matrix-v2.csv — mapping of roles to permissions and API endpoints.
- siem-export-config-example.pdf — Console screenshots and example syslog / S3 settings.
- evidence-automation-workflow.md — walkthrough showing how evidence exports are scheduled and signed.
- kms-and-encryption-summary.pdf — short doc describing encryption-at-rest and envelope keys.

Audit log schema (human-readable summary and example event):
- Required fields we include on every event: event_time (RFC3339), event_id (UUID v4), actor_id, actor_type (user|service), actor_ip, action_name, resource_type, resource_id, resource_owner, request_id, model_version, result_status (success|failure), error_code (optional), event_level (info|warning|error|security), retention_class (standard|critical).
- Optional fields: request_payload_hash, response_payload_hash, latency_ms, kv_meta (small map of indexed keys).
- Example event (single-line NDJSON example to paste into customer questionnaires):
  {"event_time":"2026-02-19T14:22:01Z","event_id":"9f8a2f3c-2d4b-4b2f-9f1a-7b6a9c0d1e2f","actor_id":"user:alice@example.com","actor_type":"user","actor_ip":"203.0.113.44","action_name":"model.deploy","resource_type":"model","resource_id":"model-7b9f","resource_owner":"org-42","request_id":"req-6b3a","model_version":"v1.3.0","result_status":"success","event_level":"info","retention_class":"standard"}

SIEM export options and recommended mappings:
- Syslog (RFC5424) over TLS: map event_time -> syslog timestamp, event_level -> severity, event_id -> message-id, remaining JSON in structured-data field.
- S3/Parquet/NDJSON: preferred for high-volume analytics; we include partition keys by project, date, level.
- CEF: we provide a translation config that maps: actor_id -> src, action_name -> name, resource_id -> cs1, model_version -> cs2, request_id -> externalId.

Automation & evidence generation workflow (operational steps):
1) Customer requests export or evidence bundle via questionnaire.
2) Solutions engineer selects the template (Hosted/Dedicated/Private) in the Playbook UI.
3) Automation service collects the most recent N files, signs the archive with an artifact signing key, and uploads to a pre-authorized S3 signed URL or pushes to customer syslog.
4) Playbook outputs a short manifest (manifest.json) listing files, checksums, and signatures for the customer to verify.
5) If policy requires additional attestation (e.g., SOC-scope evidence), SE opens a request to security-ops for manual redaction/review.

Common questionnaire Q&A (long-form suggested responses):
- Q: How do you prevent privilege escalation?
  A: RBAC v2 enforces tiered role separation and denies-by-default. Privilege elevation requests go through an approval workflow (can be automated for ephemeral access). All elevation events are logged with before/after snapshots and are reversible within the console. For Dedicated/Private deployments, customers may configure additional approval tiers through their own IDP connectors.

- Q: What controls exist to ensure logs are tamper-evident?
  A: Logs are written to append-only backends with HMAC-based write-ahead markers. Exports include signed manifests. For Private deployments, logs can be configured to stream directly to customer-managed append-only storage (WORM) or object stores with object lock enabled.

- Q: Do you collect request/response content in audit logs?
  A: Sensitive request/response bodies are not stored in full. We capture metadata, hashes, and truncated payload snippets only when necessary for debugging or security investigations and only with appropriate redaction. This is controlled by an evidence-collection policy and requires authorization for access.

Attachments checklist (for a typical SOC/ciso questionnaire):
- audit-log-sample-ndjson.txt (anonymized sample)
- rbac-role-matrix-v2.csv
- siem-export-config-example.pdf
- signed-manifest-sample.json
- retention-policy-summary.pdf

Escalation & review path (who to contact inside Redwood during question backlog):
- First-line: Solutions Engineering (se-eng@redwood.ai) — for formatting and tailoring answers.
- Security SME: Priya Nair (owner) and Marcus Lee.
- Telemetry/SRE: Hannah Ortiz for export pipeline and S3/Syslog connection validations.
- Legal/compliance: legal-security@redwood.ai for contractual evidence requests longer than 12 months or requiring special attestation.

Open items / TODOs for this playbook (notes to self):
- Add Decision Matrix for when to provide full event payload versus hash-only.
- Create a one-click console export flow mock for solution demos.
- Align retention defaults with product pricing tiers and update retention-policy-summary.pdf per pricing changes.

Notes and references: Link the customer to the full RBAC v2 design doc (linked_artifacts) and the telemetry export runbook. When in doubt about Custom SIEM parsing needs, request a sample event mapping from the customer and route to Telemetry/SRE for a quick feasibility check.

Revision history: Draft created 2026-02-20 by Priya Nair; updated 2026-03-10 with SIEM mapping table and new example event format.
